teaser:
The shop closes in ten minutes, and you are still reading the inscription inside a secondhand book, trying to work out who gave it away. Across town, someone has asked, for the third time, whether you are really all right.

You are a 7, an ISFJ, and the two rarely disagree about what matters, only about how much of it gets spoken aloud. The number asks for long private hours spent turning a question over until it yields. The type asks for a household where someone notices the coat left out in the rain and has already brought it in. Both habits can live in one person without ever quite meeting at the table.
excerpt: The radio hums low while the queue inches forward, brushes slapping rhythmically against the windshield, and neither of you says much until the car clears the line.
